triples.head: fungi
triples.evidence: As we have seen, fungi influence the well-being of human populations on a large scale because they are part of the nutrient cycle in ecosystems.

triples.head: fungi
triples.evidence: As animal pathogens, fungi help to control the population of damaging pests.

triples.head: Beauveria bassiana
triples.evidence: the fungus Beauveria bassiana is being tested as a possible biological control agent for the recent spread of emerald ash borer a beetle that feeds on ash trees.

triples.head: Beauveria bassiana
triples.evidence: It is in turn parasitized by a pathogenic fungus (Beauveria bassiana) that holds promise as a biological insecticide.

triples.head: mycorrhizal relationship
triples.evidence: The mycorrhizal relationship between fungi and plant roots is essential for the productivity of farm land.

triples.head: fungi
triples.evidence: Fermentation—of grains to produce beer, and of fruits to produce wine—is an ancient art that humans in most cultures have practiced for millennia.

triples.head: fungi
triples.evidence: Antibiotics are naturally produced by fungi to kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria, limiting their competition in the natural environment.

triples.head: fungi
triples.evidence: As simple eukaryotic organisms, fungi are important model research organisms.

triples.head: Neurospora crassa
triples.evidence: Many advances in modern genetics were achieved by the use of the red bread mold Neurospora crassa.
